questions.subject: CYBERSECURITY
questions.topic: What stops a page being framed by another origin
questions.learningObjective: Explain the mechanisms that prevent framing by another origin
questions.stem: Explain, for your projection notes, what stops a page from being placed inside a frame on another origin.

answer.exemplar: Two mechanisms do this. A framing header can name the single origin that is allowed to place the page in a frame, and a framing policy directive can list the origins that are allowed, or refuse framing altogether when it says none are permitted. Both are checked by the browser when it loads the page inside a frame, so the decision is made for the person visiting the page rather than for the page's own code, and neither needs any help from the page at run time.

questions.explanation: A strong answer names both the header and the policy directive and says who enforces them. It should note that the check happens in the browser at load time.
questions.hint: Name both mechanisms and who applies them.

questions.topic: The order that makes a path decision answerable

questions.stem: Explain, for your projection notes, why the order of decoding and checking decides whether a path check can be trusted.

answer.exemplar: A path check answers a question about the location a name refers to, so it can only be asked of the form the system will actually use. If the name is decoded after the check, the check may have examined a name that no longer matches the one that is opened, and a value that decodes a second time can change meaning between the two steps. The dependable order is therefore to interpret the name first, then check the interpreted result, and to make sure that no later step decodes it again.

questions.topic: A policy that answers with the question it was asked
questions.learningObjective: Count the rules in a policy by topic
questions.stem: A page's response carries a policy with 9 rules. 5 of the rules concern script sources, 2 concern images, 1 concerns connections, and 1 concerns framing.
questions.explanation: The rules that are not about script sources are the 2 image rules, the 1 connection rule and the 1 framing rule. Those add up to 4 rules in total.
questions.hint: Add the groups that are not about scripts.

questions.subject: CYBERSECURITY
questions.topic: Where the check belongs in an extraction routine
questions.learningObjective: Explain the cost of checking after the write

stimulus.body: The notes describe an extraction routine that reads each entry, resolves its name, writes the file, and only then checks whether the file landed inside the destination. The notes record that 3 files were found above the destination folder and were removed afterwards.

questions.stem: According to the note, what does the order of the routine cost?

options.text: Nothing, because the files were removed and the destination ended up correct
options.misconception: believes the end state settles the question

options.text: Only disk space, because the extra files are removed once they are noticed
options.misconception: reduces the cost to storage

options.text: Nothing, because the routine resolved the name before it wrote the file
options.misconception: believes resolution is the check

options.text: The check runs after the file exists, so a file outside the destination is created before anything can stop it

questions.explanation: A check after the write can report the problem but cannot prevent it, since the file outside the destination has already been created. The note's three files show the moment when the check needs to move earlier.
questions.hint: Ask what the check can do once the file exists.

questions.subject: CYBERSECURITY
questions.topic: Framing policy for a page two partners must embed
questions.learningObjective: Review a framing restriction that excludes a partner
questions.stem: You are asked to review a framing restriction for a page that two partners must embed, and the response carries only a header naming one partner.

options.text: The restriction is complete, because the second partner can be added to the header after the fact
options.misconception: assumes a header can be changed by the framer

options.text: The restriction is complete, because the header naming one origin is enough for a page used by two partners
options.misconception: ignores the second partner

options.text: The restriction is wrong because the header should name the page's own origin instead
options.misconception: redirects the header to the wrong origin

options.text: The restriction excludes one partner, so it needs a policy list naming both of them

questions.explanation: A header carries a single origin, so one of the two partners is excluded by it. A policy list is the mechanism that can name both, and it is the one that answers the requirement as stated.
questions.hint: Ask how many partners the single named origin covers.
